raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

`tokenspeed-mla` depends on `tokenspeed-triton` which uses nanobind. Upstream Triton also switched to nanobind in 3.9 (triton-lang/triton#10283). Older `tokenspeed-triton` builds register the same C++ types in nanobind's shared registry, so loading both aborts with `Critical nanobind error: refusing to add duplicate key "PAD_ZERO"`. This breaks vLLM CI on the torch 2.15 RC and nightly lanes (pytorch/test-infra#9050).

[`tokenspeed-triton` 3.9.10.post20261008](https://github.com/lightseekorg/triton/tree/release/3.9.10.post20261008) uses its own nanobind domain, so the copies no longer collide, and `tokenspeed-mla` requires it from 0.2.20. This PR bumps the `tokenspeed-mla` pin from 0.2.15 to 2.0.2 to pick up that fix.

## Claims

- Fixes the `PAD_ZERO` abort with Triton 3.9.
- Passes the TokenSpeed MLA correctness and CUDA graph tests on B200.

## Validation

All tested on one B200.

**Fixes the pytorch/test-infra#9050 repro** (torch 2.15.0 + triton 3.9.0):

| Check | 0.2.15 (tokenspeed-triton 3.8.10) | 2.0.2 (tokenspeed-triton 3.9.10) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `import triton; import tokenspeed_triton`, both orders, Python 3.11/3.12 | abort | pass |
| `test_supported_backend_preserves_dcp_eligibility[TOKENSPEED_MLA]` | abort | 1 passed |
| `test_attention_selector.py` | - | 97 passed, 14 skipped |
| Both Tritons' kernels + `torch.compile` in one process | - | pass |

**Correctness** (torch 2.13, unless noted):

| Check | 2.0.2 |
| --- | --- |
| `test_mla_backends.py -k tokenspeed_mla` (torch 2.13 and 2.15) | 307 passed, 290 skipped each |
| TokenSpeed decode tests (accuracy, CUDA graphs, split-KV) | 203 passed, 77 skipped (SM107) |
| Accuracy and CUDA graphs with both Tritons loaded (torch 2.15) | 63 passed |
| Additional FP8 reference cases | 16 passed |
| GSM8K, eager x2 | 0.7771, 0.7801 |
| GSM8K, CUDA graphs x2 | 0.7718, 0.7756 |

All four GSM8K runs passed. The model was `RedHatAI/DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct-FP8`, with 1,319 questions, five-shot, seed 42 and temperature 0.

**Installs correctly:** `uv pip compile` picks `tokenspeed-triton==3.9.10.post20261008` on the default and nightly indexes. `pre-commit` passes; `requirements/test/cuda.txt` is unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

B200 (sm100), driver 580.82.07, CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12. torch 2.15 env: torch 2.15.0+cu130 and triton 3.9.0 from `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/test/cu130`; vLLM via `tools/use_existing_torch.py` and `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1`.

Tests used vLLM snapshot `b48ae0e6` and matching precompiled artifacts from its main parent `624a5dda`. Model evaluations used torch 2.13; torch 2.15 covered imports, selectors and kernels. Python 3.11 coverage is limited to compiler imports.

```bash
python -c "import triton; import tokenspeed_triton"
python -c "import tokenspeed_triton; import triton"
pytest -v "tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py::test_supported_backend_preserves_dcp_eligibility[TOKENSPEED_MLA]"
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_attention_selector.py
pytest -v tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k tokenspeed_mla
pytest -s tests/evals/gsm8k/test_gsm8k_correctness.py --config-list-file=<list>
# lightseekorg/tokenspeed at the release commit:
pytest -v tokenspeed-mla/tests/test_mla_decode.py
```

GSM8K server args: `--max-model-len 4096 --attention-backend TOKENSPEED_MLA --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --block-size 64`, plus `--enforce-eager` for the eager runs. Model revision: `efe1ced428db63e7ccbcf367334596f77e9af140`.

</details>

## Details

**Changes from 0.2.15 to 2.0.2:**

- The fixed `tokenspeed-triton` sets `NB_DOMAIN=tokenspeed` (lightseekorg/tokenspeed#2134).
- Also picks up lightseekorg/tokenspeed#2132 (0.2.20), which fixes an illegal memory access in decode when `tokenspeed_mla_min_split_kv` > 1 produces 256 MiB or more of partials.
- DCP visibility/masking and empty-shard output/LSE handling (0.2.16, lightseekorg/tokenspeed#1853), plus decode synchronization and zero-tile guards. The added `local_visible_lens` argument defaults to `None`; vLLM does not pass it.
- CuTe DSL 4.8 compatibility cleanup (0.2.17, lightseekorg/tokenspeed#2048), compatible with vLLM's existing CUTLASS DSL pin.
- An SM107 FP8-output decode path (0.2.18, lightseekorg/tokenspeed#2060) and subsequent scheduling/softmax tuning (2.0.1, lightseekorg/tokenspeed#2213). vLLM's current B200 call uses BF16 output and does not select this path. SM107 runtime changes were not tested here.
- Unused helper cleanup (lightseekorg/tokenspeed#2278). Existing vLLM decode/prefill calls remain compatible.
- Authored with assistance from Codex.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>
